pages.title: What we are building
pages.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: OPDA semantic-modelling section header for /semantic-modelling/understand/what-we-are-building.
Primary request: Create ONE original wide 3:1 three-panel sequential ink narrative for adults. It tells one restrained left-to-right story about one agreement being inspectable through different views. The same two credible adult property professionals must be unmistakably retained in all three panels: a middle-aged Black woman building surveyor with short natural hair, petrol work jacket and coral scarf; and a white man in his late fifties with silver hair, round spectacles and violet overshirt. Their faces, clothes and proportions remain consistent across the strip.
Scene/backdrop: grounded British dwelling-inspection work, on cool off-white #F9F9F9 paper to every canvas edge. No decorative or abstract background.
Panel one: at the entrance hall of a modest British dwelling after an inspection, the surveyor poses one clear ordinary-language question through natural questioning gesture and attention toward a visibly closed interior door; the colleague studies the same doorway and a plain clipboard. Do not use a speech bubble or any writing.
Panel two: at a worktable, those same two adults compare two visibly distinct original source artefacts about that one inspection: one substantial report document with blank ruled strokes and one separate architectural floor-plan sheet with drawn room shapes but absolutely no labels, letters, numbers or symbols. Both originals are clearly separate and neither is treated as the winner.
Panel three: those same two adults annotate a third draft comparison sheet between them, using only non-readable freehand marks and shaded areas; both distinct original report and floorplan remain fully visible and physically separate beside the draft; a second small blank alternative draft card remains set aside and visibly unresolved. Their expressions are thoughtful, provisional and professionally engaged, never celebratory.
Style/medium: elegant crisp brush-and-pen drawing with expressive deep-purple #231F2F contours and flat pastel opaque gouache fields; sophisticated adult editorial illustration; subtle dry-brush grain only; explicitly NOT watercolour, not a children's cartoon, not caricature, not comic-book action styling.
Composition/framing: exact full 3:1 panoramic canvas, three equal shallow panels read left to right, separated by thin simple deep-purple gutters. Fill the strip with full subjects and complete props, no cropped heads or hands, no huge blank margins. Each panel is a distinct moment but the horizontal rhythm is cohesive and calm. Crisp and legible at 1200x400.
Color palette: cool off-white #F9F9F9 paper, deep-purple ink #231F2F, generous flat OPDA gold #FEC92B, petrol #0E8478, violet #6C5BD4, restrained coral accents. No beige or sepia cast.
Meaning constraints: show one agreement inspected through different views, not six competing models. The illustration is a fictional teaching scene, not evidence. Human discussion does not prove truth. Do not depict an operational application, automatic pipeline, approved outcome, consensus, green tick, checkmark, approval stamp or final truth.
Text constraints: absolutely NO embedded text of any kind: no words, letters, numbers, labels, speech bubbles, captions, signage, icons, symbols or arrows. Documents may contain only loose non-semantic blank strokes and areas, never text-like glyphs.
Avoid: logos, watermarks, floating nodes, linked-network motifs, glow, neon, gradients, photography, glossy 3D, UI chrome, giant empty margins, extra people, extra panels, duplicated limbs or malformed hands. Full artwork only.
